cat.user-temp.name: Your temporary files
cat.user-temp.what: Files programs and installers leave in your Temp folder.
cat.user-temp.safe: Only files untouched for 2 days are removed, and files a program still holds open are skipped.
cat.windows-temp.name: Windows temporary files
cat.windows-temp.what: Files Windows services and installers leave in the Windows Temp folder.
cat.windows-temp.safe: Only files untouched for 2 days are removed, and files in use are skipped.
cat.crash-dumps.name: Crash dumps
cat.crash-dumps.what: Memory snapshots saved when a program crashed.
cat.crash-dumps.safe: They are only useful to a developer investigating that crash. Dumps from the last 7 days are kept in case you want to report one.
cat.error-reports.name: Windows error reports
cat.error-reports.what: Problem reports Windows collected about programs that stopped working.
cat.error-reports.safe: Reports already sent or older than 7 days are not needed again. Reliability Monitor keeps its own summary.
cat.error-reports-all.name: Windows error reports (all users)
cat.error-reports-all.what: Problem reports collected for services and other users.
cat.error-reports-all.safe: Reports older than 7 days are not needed again.
cat.thumbnails-win.name: Thumbnail cache
cat.thumbnails-win.what: Small previews of pictures and videos that File Explorer saved.
cat.thumbnails-win.safe: File Explorer makes them again when you open a folder. Files it holds open are skipped.
cat.thumbnails-win.cost: Folders full of pictures show blank previews for a moment the next time.
cat.thumbnails-unix.name: Thumbnail cache
cat.thumbnails-unix.what: Small previews of pictures and videos the file manager saved.
cat.thumbnails-unix.safe: Previews not looked at for 30 days are removed; they are made again when needed.
cat.browser.name: {{browser}} cache
cat.browser.what: Copies of pages, images and scripts {{browser}} saved to load sites faster.
cat.browser.safe: The browser rebuilds its cache as you browse. History, passwords, cookies, open tabs and sign-ins are not touched.
cat.browser.cost: Sites you visit often load a little slower the first time afterwards.
cat.recycle-bin.name: Recycle Bin
cat.recycle-bin.what: Files you deleted. They stay in the Recycle Bin until it is emptied.
cat.recycle-bin.safe: Only empty it when you are sure you will not want any of them back.
cat.recycle-bin.cost: Files in it can no longer be restored.
cat.trash.name: Trash
cat.trash.what: Files you deleted. They stay in the trash until it is emptied.
cat.trash.safe: Only empty it when you are sure you will not want any of them back.
cat.trash.cost: Files in it can no longer be restored.
health.space.title: Free space on {{drive}}
health.space.advice.problem: Windows needs free space for updates, the page file and temporary files. Clean caches, then look at your largest files.
health.space.advice.attention: Getting low. Cleaning caches and old downloads usually gives back several gigabytes.
health.memory.title: Memory in use
health.memory.advice: Memory is nearly full, so Windows is moving data to disk, which feels slow. Close programs you are not using, or turn off startup programs you do not need. Tools that "free RAM" only empty Windows' own cache, which makes things slower afterwards.
health.uptime.title: Time since last restart
health.uptime.advice: Restarting finishes installing updates and clears programs that slowly use more memory. With Fast Startup on, shutting down is not a restart: choose Restart.
health.av.title: Virus protection
health.av.unknown: Kempt could not read the protection status.
health.av.off.advice: Turn it back on in Windows Security. It is free and built in; no extra antivirus is needed.
health.av.stale_one: Microsoft Defender is on, but its virus definitions are {{count}} day old.
health.av.stale_other: Microsoft Defender is on, but its virus definitions are {{count}} days old.
health.av.stale.advice: Connect to the internet and run Windows Update; definitions normally update every day.
health.av.ok: Microsoft Defender is on; definitions are {{age}} old.
health.firewall.title: Firewall
health.firewall.advice: The Windows firewall blocks unwanted incoming connections. Turn it on unless another firewall replaces it.
health.disk.title: Drive health: {{name}}
health.disk.warning: The drive reports early signs of failure ({{status}}). Back up your files now, then plan to replace it.
health.disk.unhealthy: The drive reports that it is failing ({{status}}). Copy your important files somewhere else today.
health.reboot.title: Restart needed
health.reboot.detail: Windows has installed updates that finish on the next restart.
health.reboot.advice: Save your work and restart when convenient.
health.updates.title: Windows updates
health.updates.advice: Windows normally installs security updates every month. Check Windows Update for anything stuck or paused.
health.battery.title: Battery wear
health.battery.detail: The battery holds {{percent}} of its original charge.
health.battery.advice: A battery below about 60% of its design capacity runs out much sooner. Replacing it restores the running time; software cannot.
health.storagesense.title: Storage Sense
health.storagesense.detail: Off. Storage Sense is Windows' own automatic cleanup of temporary files and the Recycle Bin.
health.storagesense.advice: Turning it on is a good, free complement to Kempt.
health.repair.title: System file check
health.repair.detail: If Windows itself misbehaves (settings that will not open, crashes in Windows components), its own repair tools check every system file against a known-good copy.
health.repair.advice: This runs System File Checker and DISM in a window you can watch. It takes 10 to 30 minutes and needs administrator rights.
priv.advertising-id.title: Advertising ID
priv.advertising-id.what: Lets apps use an ID for this account to show you personalised ads.
priv.language-list.title: Websites see your language list
priv.language-list.what: Lets websites read the languages you use, to show local content.
priv.app-launch-tracking.title: Track the apps you open
priv.app-launch-tracking.what: Windows records which apps you start to improve Start and search results.
priv.tailored.title: Tailored experiences
priv.tailored.what: Microsoft uses your diagnostic data to show tips, ads and recommendations.
priv.settings-suggestions.title: Suggestions in Settings
priv.settings-suggestions.what: Shows suggested content and offers inside the Settings app.
priv.start-suggestions.title: Suggestions in Start
priv.start-suggestions.what: Shows recommended apps and promotions in the Start menu.
priv.tips.title: Tips and suggestions
priv.tips.what: Notifications with tips, tricks and suggestions while you use Windows.
priv.welcome.title: Welcome screens after updates
priv.welcome.what: After some updates, a full-screen page shows what is new and suggests Microsoft services.
priv.lockscreen-tips.title: Fun facts and tips on the lock screen
priv.lockscreen-tips.what: Adds text, tips and promotions over the lock screen picture.
priv.silent-installs.title: Automatically install suggested apps
priv.silent-installs.what: Windows may install promoted apps and games for this account on its own. There is no switch for this in Settings.
journal.repair: Started System File Checker and DISM

journal.autostart.off: Kempt no longer starts when you sign in
journal.minimized.on: Kempt opens minimized on the taskbar at startup
journal.minimized.off: Kempt opens its window normally at startup

err.app.read: Could not read the startup setting.
err.autostart.unsupported: Starting with the computer is not available on this system.
err.minimize.unsupported: Opening minimized is only available on Windows.
err.elevate.already: Kempt is already running with the rights it can have.
err.elevate.unsupported: Run Kempt with sudo to clean folders that belong to the system.
err.windowsOnly: This is only available on Windows.
err.folder.isFile: That is a file, not a folder.
err.recycle.notSearched: Kempt only moves files it showed you in a search.
err.winget.missing: winget is not installed. Install App Installer from the Microsoft Store to check for updates.
err.startup.read: Could not read the startup programs.
err.startup.needsAdmin: This program starts for every user of this computer. Restart Kempt as administrator to change it.
err.startup.notFound: That startup item no longer exists.
err.privacy.unsupported: Privacy settings are only available on Windows.
err.schedule.unsupported: Automatic care uses Windows Task Scheduler and is only available on Windows.
err.schedule.day: Choose a day of the week.
err.reveal.refused: Kempt only opens folders of files it showed you.
app.restarting.text: A new Kempt window opens in a moment. You can close this one.
nav.label: Sections
err.offline: Kempt has stopped. Open it again from the Start menu or its shortcut.
overview.title: Your PC, as it is
overview.lede: Kempt measures, explains what it found and changes nothing until you say so.
overview.startup_one: {{count}} program starts when you sign in
overview.startup_other: {{count}} programs start when you sign in
overview.startup.sub: Each one adds to the wait before your desktop is ready. Turn off the ones you do not need right away.
overview.bin.sub: Kempt never empties it on its own. Empty it when you are sure you will not want those files back.
overview.nothing: Nothing needs your attention right now.
overview.ribbon.label: Drive {{drive}}: {{used}} used, {{go}} of it can go, {{free}} free
overview.canGo: of caches and leftovers can go without losing anything you made.
overview.covers_one: Covers {{count}} kind of file, chosen in Automatic care.
overview.covers_other: Covers {{count}} kinds of files, chosen in Automatic care.
receipt.skipped_one: {{count}} file was left because a program was using it.
receipt.skipped_other: {{count}} files were left because a program was using them.
clean.title: Clean up
clean.lede: Caches and leftovers that programs recreate on their own. Your documents, photos, passwords, cookies and browsing history are never part of this.
clean.confirmBin: Empty the {{bin}}? Files in it cannot be restored afterwards.
clean.diskCleanup.title: Windows Update leftovers and old Windows versions
clean.diskCleanup.text: Windows’ own Disk Cleanup knows which of these are safe to remove. Choose “Clean up system files” there.
clean.leftAlone.days_one: Files changed in the last {{count}} day.
clean.leftAlone.days_other: Files changed in the last {{count}} days.
large.title: Large files
large.lede: The biggest files in a folder, so you can decide what you still need. Programs, Windows and app data are left out of the search.
large.none_one: No files that large among {{count}} file.
large.none_other: No files that large among {{count}} files.
dupes.title: Duplicates
dupes.lede: Files with exactly the same contents, compared byte for byte. Kempt marks the oldest copy to keep; you choose which copies go.
dupes.keepOne: Keep at least one copy of every file: {{path}}
dupes.summary_one: {{count}} set of duplicates, {{size}} in extra copies
dupes.summary_other: {{count}} sets of duplicates, {{size}} in extra copies
startup.title: Startup
startup.lede: Programs that start when you sign in. Kempt uses the same switch as Task Manager, so turning one off is always reversible and nothing is deleted.
startup.lede.unix: Programs that start when you sign in, from the autostart folders. Turning one off writes a personal override; nothing is deleted.
startup.none: No programs start when you sign in.
startup.willStart: {{name}} will start when you sign in.
startup.willNotStart: {{name}} will no longer start when you sign in.
startup.note: Changes take effect the next time you sign in.
startup.note.win: Task Manager and Settings › Apps › Startup show the same state.
updates.title: App updates
updates.lede: Kempt asks winget, the package manager built into Windows, which of your programs have a newer version, and installs them from the same sources Microsoft uses.
updates.noWinget: winget is missing. It comes with App Installer from the Microsoft Store; install or update that, then open this page again.
updates.checking: Asking winget for updates. This can take a minute…
updates.none: Every program winget knows about is up to date.
updates.progress: Updating {{name}}… ({{done}} of {{total}} done). Some installers ask for permission.
updates.truncated: Name too long for winget’s list; update it from the program itself
health.title: Health
health.lede: The things that decide whether this PC is in good shape: space, drives, protection, updates and memory. No made-up score.
health.memoryNote: Memory a program holds is not wasted. It only matters when memory is nearly full; then close what you are not using.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: Switches Windows keeps for your account. Kempt changes the same values the Settings app does, and each one links to its page there.
privacy.note: Some changes show after you sign out and in again. Every change is in History, where you can undo it.
care.title: Automatic care
care.lede: Kempt can tidy the same caches on a schedule, using Windows Task Scheduler. Nothing of Kempt runs in the background in between.
care.saved: Saved. Tidy up and automatic care use these kinds.
care.adminOnly: Only when Kempt runs as administrator
care.whatNote: Also used by Tidy up on the overview. The {{bin}} is never emptied automatically, and anything a program has open is skipped.
care.cron: Scheduling uses Windows Task Scheduler. On this system, add this line to your crontab (crontab -e) for a weekly run on Sunday at 11:00:
care.moved: If you move Kempt to another folder, save this again so the task finds it.
settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: How Kempt itself starts, and its language. Starting with Windows is off unless you turn it on.
settings.startup.on: Kempt will start when you sign in.
settings.startup.off: Kempt will no longer start when you sign in.
settings.startup.sub.win: Kempt opens when you sign in to Windows. It is listed as “Kempt” under Startup, here and in Task Manager, and nothing is cleaned until you ask.
settings.startup.sub.unix: Kempt opens when you sign in. It adds one file, kempt.desktop, to your autostart folder.
settings.minimized: Minimize to desktop and stick to taskbar
settings.minimized.on: Kempt will open minimized on the taskbar at startup.
settings.minimized.off: Kempt will open its window normally at startup.
settings.minimized.sub: When Kempt starts with Windows, its window opens minimized and stays on the taskbar until you click it.
settings.minimized.needsStartup: Turn on Start at Windows startup first.
settings.note: Closing the window still closes Kempt. Changes to how Kempt starts are recorded in History.
history.title: History
history.lede: Everything Kempt changed, newest first. Startup and privacy changes can be undone here.
history.empty: Nothing yet. Every change Kempt makes will be listed here.
why.title: What Kempt won’t do
why.lede: All-in-one “PC optimizers” bundle many features. Some help; these do not, so Kempt leaves them out.
why.registry.title: Clean the registry
why.registry.text: Unused registry entries take a few kilobytes and do not slow Windows down. Removing the wrong one can break a program or Windows itself, and Microsoft does not support registry cleaners (support article KB2563254).
why.ram.title: “Free up” or “boost” RAM
why.ram.text: Windows fills spare memory with a cache of files you are likely to open next and gives it back the instant a program needs it. Emptying it makes the next things you open slower. When memory really is full, the fix is to close programs or turn off ones that start with Windows, which Kempt shows you.
why.internet.title: Speed up your internet by 300%
why.internet.text: Windows has tuned its network settings automatically since Windows Vista. Your connection speed is set by your provider, your Wi-Fi signal and the site you visit, not by a setting a tool can change.
why.drivers.title: Update drivers from its own database
why.drivers.text: Third-party driver updaters can install the wrong driver for your hardware. Windows Update delivers drivers tested for your PC, and your PC maker’s support page has the rest.
why.score.title: Give your PC a score or an “AI mode”
why.score.text: A single number hides what is going on. Kempt shows each measurement with what it means and what to do about it.
why.antivirus.title: Replace your antivirus
why.antivirus.text: Microsoft Defender is built in, updates itself and is enough for most people. Kempt checks that it, or the antivirus you chose, is switched on.
why.background.title: Run in the background or nag you to upgrade
why.background.text: Kempt runs only while its window is open, or when the task you scheduled starts it. It starts with Windows only if you turn that on in Settings. There is no paid version, no advertising and no data sent anywhere.
